content: Coxsackie virus is a cytolytic virus that belongs to the Picornaviridae family and is classified as an enterovirus. Enteroviruses include polioviruses, coxsackieviruses, and echoviruses. Among the 61 non-polio enteroviruses that are known to cause disease in humans, 23 are classified as Coxsackie A viruses, while 6 are classified as Coxsackie B viruses. Enteroviruses are the second most common viral pathogens in humans, surpassed only by rhinoviruses. Coxsackie viruses are divided into two main groups: Coxsackie A viruses and Coxsackie B viruses. The Coxsackie B viruses are further categorized into six serotypes, one of which is the Coxsackie B4 virus, a serotype of particular clinical significance. Coxsackie A and B viruses are capable of causing a wide range of diseases in humans. These diseases can be distinguished from one another based on the organ systems involved, the clinical manifestations, and the diagnostic methods employed. For example, oral lesions caused by Coxsackie virus infections must be differentiated from other conditions that cause similar oral lesions, such as oral candidiasis and aphthous ulcers. When oral involvement is suspected, it is critical to differentiate Coxsackie virus-induced lesions from other diseases that present with oral lesions, such as leukoplakia or infections caused by the herpes simplex virus.
